correctness.rationale: PASS: For the multiplicative alternating divisor sum beta(p^e)=(p^(e+1)+(-1)^e)/(p+1), 4 beta(n)=n implies v2(n)>=2. If at most six distinct prime factors, n=2^a times at most five odd-prime powers. Each odd p contributes beta(p^e)/p^e >=(p-1)/p, minimized over five odd primes at 3,5,7,11,13 with product 384/1001. At a=2 the dyadic factor 3/4 yields 288/1001>1/4; at a=4 it is 11/16 yielding 264/1001>1/4; for a>=5 it is at least 21/32 yielding 252/1001>1/4. At a=3, beta(8)=5 is odd and v2(beta(n))=a-2=1, so exactly one odd prime has odd exponent. This factor is at least (p-1)/p, every remaining even-exponent prime factor at least p/(p+1). The minimum among five odd primes occurs with the exceptional odd exponent on p=3 and four other smallest possible odd primes 5,7,11,13, giving (5/8)(2/3)(5/6)(7/8)(11/12)(13/14)=3575/13824>1/4. Contradiction for all cases with omega(n)<=6. All fractions independently checked with exact rational arithmetic and original checker source inspected. No existence/sharpness claim.
